title: Arcanea: The Sovereign Depths
subtitle: Ancient power. Living worlds. Consequences that remain.
description: Twenty-four proposed boss encounters across twelve materially distinct dungeons, authored for adult cinematic fantasy, interconnected novels and readable encounter design. This is a staged creative collection, not an assertion of implemented playable game systems.

source.commitPurpose: Pinned canon baseline; all collection records are new local proposals.

series.title: The Kiln and the Keel
series.continuity: Standalone proposed trilogy; separate from the Chronicles and Living Arc.
series.premise: Engineer Tamsin Reed and shipwright Garrick Moss try to reopen a winter harbour, discover its material supply has been captured by a coordinated blockade campaign, and turn the occupiers’ production timetable against them.

cast.name: Tamsin Reed
cast.want: Rebuild a harbour that can survive winter without accepting military ownership.
cast.pressure: Each fast material solution repeats a destructive practice she promised the workers would end.

cast.name: Garrick Moss
cast.want: Bring the pressed shipwrights home alive.
cast.pressure: He will trade away long-term independence for a rescue today, putting him at odds with Tamsin.

books.title: The Heat We Inherit
books.premise: A contract for winter anchors sends the pair into a still-burning foundry. They discover that the same alloy is supplying a mountain gun, and their choice of furnace output determines whether they can follow that shipment in time.

books.title: Under a Broken Sun
books.premise: The mountain road is blocked by obsolete artillery and a captain trying to claim it. Saving a stranded evacuation column costs the pair their best transport window but yields the blockade’s launch schedule.

books.title: The Harbour That Refused
books.premise: The shipwrights sabotage their own launch work while Tamsin turns recovered components into a controlled premature launch. Liberation succeeds only if the harbour predator is given a quiet exit and the workers keep command of the rebuilt arsenal.

series.title: The Passage Compact
series.continuity: Standalone proposed trilogy; no replacement for existing flagship book sequences.
series.premise: Diver Brigid Vale and cargo assessor Isen Pike seek a winter passage for a struggling coast. Their journey moves from a drowned military obstruction to disputed seed custody and finally a public trial over the route’s governance.

cast.name: Brigid Vale
cast.want: Establish a reliable winter route that ordinary crews can navigate.
cast.pressure: She can survive hazards that the people following her cannot, so personal bravery is an insufficient plan.

cast.name: Isen Pike
cast.want: Keep promises measurable enough to survive changes of leadership.
cast.pressure: His precise contracts cannot substitute for trust when a living cargo begins to die.

books.title: The Current Below
books.premise: The divers reopen a starved reef inlet and recover evidence of a refused evacuation. Their new route reaches a mountain trade station whose seed stock may save the coastal harvest.

books.title: A Winter Held in Glass
books.premise: Two expeditions must agree on custody while the seed vault thaws around them. Brigid’s rivalry with Kethrane becomes a workable alliance only when both crews accept visible losses and shared transport obligations.

books.title: The Measure of Passage
books.premise: The mountain court can open the final route, but its old apparatus contradicts the terms of a fair trial. Brigid wins a passage and accepts a public maintenance duty, making the compact more durable than her own reputation.

series.title: The Living Meridian
series.continuity: Independent proposed expedition trilogy; observed ecology is distinguished from disputed mythology.
series.premise: Surveyor Corvin Holt and financier Fenwick Darr follow a promised mineral route through forest, crater and desert. Each discovery changes what their contract can honestly claim, until a water observation must become public knowledge rather than the venture’s private asset.

cast.name: Corvin Holt
cast.want: Publish a map people can use without discovering its omissions through death.
cast.pressure: The expedition deadline rewards confident simplification of conditions that keep changing.

cast.name: Fenwick Darr
cast.want: Return enough value to keep his crew employed.
cast.pressure: A lower-yield truthful contract threatens his solvency, while an inflated claim would finance the next expedition immediately.

books.title: The Line Through Leaves
books.premise: A disputed crossing forces the surveyors to face an equally competent rival. Evidence of altered mineral growth beyond the frontier makes Serevra a necessary independent witness rather than a defeated obstacle.

books.title: The Forest in the Stone
books.premise: A living mineral seam promises the expedition’s fortune until extraction accelerates a parasite outbreak. Fenwick must sign a lower-yield contract before knowing whether it will save his company.

books.title: The Water Under Stars
books.premise: The desert observation can validate the new route, but a scholar seeks exclusive control of the result. Corvin and Fenwick establish independent measurements during a colossal migration and publish the water map, earning a different business through trustworthy passage services.

series.title: The Unfinished Road
series.continuity: Standalone proposed investigation trilogy; experimental Lacuna chapters remain explicitly opt-in.
series.premise: Archivist Sabine Rook and surveyor Jolant Grey follow evidence of a campaign intended to isolate the frontier. They must preserve testimony, publish bounded uncertainty and use incomplete records fast enough to save a convoy.

cast.name: Sabine Rook
cast.want: Keep ordinary witnesses in the record of a war written by its commanders.
cast.pressure: She cannot physically rescue every object, and choosing what to carry has irreversible consequences.

cast.name: Jolant Grey
cast.want: Recover missing surveyors and prove a safe road exists.
cast.pressure: He must put his name to a useful account that leaves the chamber’s deepest cause unresolved.

books.title: Names in the Quiet Bell
books.premise: An occupied burial avenue hides a siege calibration method. Saving the quieter annex yields supply references to a vanished road survey, while destroying it leaves a faster but less provable trail.

books.title: A Stair Without an Answer
books.premise: The missing surveyors are trapped in a bounded impossible chamber. Their recovery provides an alternate exterior road plan; Jolant refuses to invent an origin story to make the report seem complete.

books.title: The Road at the Edge
books.premise: Records from the bells, survey and harbour campaign reveal a local bridge interdiction. Sabine and Jolant use that knowledge to protect a frontier convoy, ending at the exterior road with Malachar’s prison untouched.

canonPolicy.approvedBaseline: Existing identities and events are compatibility constraints; local proposals are never inherited as APPROVED.
canonPolicy.gates: No additional Gate, bonded Godbeast or divine identity is introduced.
canonPolicy.origins: No new Origin class is introduced. Fauna labels describe ecology; they do not assign a metaphysical Origin.
canonPolicy.nero: Nero remains the fertile unknown and potential, not evil. Local uncertainty and spatial danger do not imply moral darkness.
canonPolicy.shadowfen: Malachar remains sealed. The exterior finale never enters, depicts, opens or weakens his canonical prison.
canonPolicy.continuities: The four proposed trilogies are separate from the established Chronicles and the staged Living Arc. Cross-series links are optional shared-world events, not an imposed reading order.
canonPolicy.experimentalRetrieval: EXPERIMENTAL records and any story using them require explicit opt-in; links do not promote their authority.
canonPolicy.power: Scale, combat threat, political authority and magical attainment are separate; no body size implies Gate rank.
canonPolicy.names: All names remain working proposals pending repository-wide naming and rights review.

crossSeriesLinks.event: Seized Blackwake launch orders establish that the harbour blockade and outer-road interdiction are parts of one operation.
crossSeriesLinks.ordering: The orders may reach Sabine by courier; neither book requires the other as prerequisite reading.

crossSeriesLinks.event: The Passage Compact can carry water-route survey records between coast and desert after both independent stories resolve.
crossSeriesLinks.ordering: An optional epilogue connection; no fixed inter-series chronology is asserted.

crossSeriesLinks.event: Serevra returns as an independent witness to the mineral claim, retaining her expedition and leverage.
crossSeriesLinks.ordering: Causal within The Living Meridian; her survival and relationship state must be selected for a novel continuity.

crossSeriesLinks.event: Kethrane testifies to the seed-custody agreement at the passage court.
crossSeriesLinks.ordering: Novel continuity assumes a negotiated or honourably resolved bridge encounter; game alternatives remain separate branches.

adaptationPolicy.novels: Each novel selects one authored sequence and preserves its consequences. Do not print player HUD language, objective counters or every optional branch into the prose.
adaptationPolicy.games: Encounter phases are design specifications with observable tells, counters and persistent failure states. Implement and playtest separately before claiming balance or playability.
adaptationPolicy.agents: Retrieve baseline and proposals by explicit status and scope. A reference, title, link, image or merged proposal is not canon approval.
adaptationPolicy.visuals: Individual images illustrate a selected dramatic moment, not an exact mechanics diagram. Stable anatomy and materials carry across art, prose and future game assets.

factions.name: Cinder Mutual
factions.purpose: A workshop coalition contracting for winter anchors and keeping production decisions with the people doing the work.
factions.resource: Foundry skill, salvage agreements and labour consent.
factions.internalConflict: Some members favour a fast military contract to keep households fed; others regard that dependence as the beginning of occupation.

factions.name: Tide Witness crews
factions.purpose: Independent divers documenting safe seasonal passage and recoverable evidence from drowned sites.
factions.resource: Air bells, current charts and repeated field observations.
factions.internalConflict: A fast elite route can earn money immediately while remaining unusable by ordinary crews.

factions.name: Meridian Survey
factions.purpose: A commercial expedition partnership mapping mineral and transport claims.
factions.resource: Contracts, transport capacity and independent witnesses.
factions.internalConflict: Reliable lower-yield findings threaten short-term solvency; spectacular unverified claims attract financing.

factions.name: Pale Line expedition
factions.purpose: Serevra’s autonomous canopy crew, defending the rescue infrastructure its members rebuilt.
factions.resource: Local route knowledge, rope work and a defensible access claim.
factions.internalConflict: Protecting the crew’s claim can become exclusion of people who also need rescue.

factions.name: White Vigil expedition
factions.purpose: Kethrane’s seed-recovery crew, accountable to its workers and a sponsor with competing custody demands.
factions.resource: Controlled warming expertise and the first viable transport route.
factions.internalConflict: Sponsor ownership terms conflict with the crew’s wish to distribute viable stock.

factions.name: Void Ascendant blockade campaign
factions.purpose: A new local operation of an existing antagonistic faction, seeking to isolate the frontier by sea and road.
factions.resource: Captured furnace output, artillery sites, pressed shipwrights and an exterior siege working.
factions.internalConflict: Operators compete over scarce shipments and priority; their local tactics frequently obstruct each other.
